recommended.why: The most direct answer to "trading today" — whether the storefront was reachable when the record was ordered.
You asked for the domain. This is the one that ties the registrant back to this business rather than to a reseller or a parked holder.
Says whether the domain came from the customer or was found independently — a supplied URL proves less than a discovered one.
Connects the storefront to the premises: the address on the site matching the submitted one is what makes the two the same operation.
The site naming this business, rather than a different trading entity behind the same domain.
Your mailbox question, answered most sharply. Five addresses shared with 101 or more businesses is the signature of a registered-agent or mail-forwarding address.
The counterweight: addresses shared with only a handful of businesses read as genuinely occupied premises.
Commercial versus residential — a mailbox is commercial too, so this narrows rather than settles it, and is worth reading beside the frequency bands.
Not currently read by this assessment. The submitted address matching an address on a state registration is the strongest non-web evidence that the premises is the one the business filed under.
A reachable third-party profile is corroboration of trading that does not depend on the company's own website being up.
